react_result.final_narrative_text: The metabolomics comparison between control and treatment groups reveals a pronounced enrichment of arachidonic acid metabolism as the dominant pathway, confirmed across complementary analytical paradigms. Mummichog network-based enrichment (empirical-compound m/z-direct) identified arachidonic acid metabolism as the top-ranked pathway (p = 0.0051, overlap = 11/11 compounds hit), with the same chemical family producing four additional significant pathway hits: prostaglandin formation from arachidonate (rank 4, p = 0.0448), leukotriene metabolism (rank 5, p = 0.0448), glycerophospholipid metabolism (rank 3, p = 0.0297), and vitamin A (retinol) metabolism as a co-enriched contextual pathway (rank 2, p = 0.0217). The six driver metabolites driving this module are arachidonic acid (KEGG:C00219), leukotriene A4 (C00909), 15-deoxy-Δ12,14-prostaglandin J2 (C14717), 5-HETE (C04805), and 15-HETE (C04742). The InChIKey reconciliation confirmed all nine input metabolites are structurally distinct and unambiguous — no naming conflicts or ID collisions were detected, ruling out namespace artefacts as an explanation for the enrichment signal. Xanthine (C00385) and methylmalonic acid (C02170) did not map to the arachidonic acid cluster but likely contribute through independent purine and odd-chain fatty acid threads. 5-Androstenediol (C04295) anchors a separate steroid hormone biosynthesis signal (rank 7, p = 0.065). The convergent arachidonic acid / eicosanoid interpretation is the dominant biological story: the treatment group shows coordinated deregulation of lipoxygenase and cyclooxygenase branch products, consistent with an inflammatory or bioactive lipid signaling response.
